sources.title: Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too

comments.author: tarruda
comments.text: I wonder how far this can be taken. Could Qwen 3.8 can interpret and make improvements to Qwen 3.5 0.8B weights, or even its own weights?

comments.author: athrowaway3z
comments.text: Hopefully we get a new benchmark: How well can a model tweak a set of weights to produce pelican on a bike?

comments.author: layer8
comments.text: > I’m not ready to declare that the age of source code is over and our future involves incomprehensible machines editing their own model weights in incomprehensible ways. That sounds a bit like biology; maybe AI will become like that.

comments.author: bsiverly
comments.text: Wasn’t this one of the main marketing points for the Inkling model as well?

comments.author: variaga
comments.text: Not making any claims about a specific model's capabilities, but all these "can interpret model weights" posts brings to mind the line in Shakespeare's Henry IV GLENDOWE: I can call spirits from the vasty deep. HOTSPUR: Why, so can I, or so can any man, but will they come when you do call for them? I can interpret…

comments.author: spwa4
comments.text: OpenAI is also now hiding your usage. Not accessible anymore in the menu, and /usage in the codex app now also gives a lot of stats, but the one stat you do want to know, how much limit left, is no longer there. I'm guessing another big usage reduction is coming soon.

comments.author: monster_truck
comments.text: If your company actually cared about this they would be running their own inference instead of leaving fate to a couple of checkboxes.

comments.author: CEOatMindfries
comments.text: May be the coding agents should build a layer when they don't leak any IP, treat them like environment variables, which must be handled deterministically.

comments.author: edot
comments.text: Turn on advanced account security. You should be doing this anyways (requires hardware keys). But it also locks data sharing off.
